# `reduct.theodolite()` {#fn-reduct-theodolite}

W02 recovered both independent circle-difference control bearings and retained each site row in a multi-site solar reduction. [W02 results](w02-field-to-sky.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-reduct-theodolite)

```{=html}
<p>The observed difference between the instrument readings to the structure and to the Sun
is added to the calculated solar azimuth at the observation time. The routine handles a
circle-boundary difference, accounts for the selected solar limb through sunAz and
rounds the reference bearing according to the input readings. An explicit altitude or a
supplied horizon allows the corrected bearing to be converted to declination. Correct
time, civil timezone, limb and site are all essential to the reduction.
</p>
<p>Astronomical positions require Swiss Ephemeris files covering the epoch. We
recommend installing <span class="pkg">swephRdata</span>; see <code>skyscapeR-package</code> for setup.
</p>
```

<details><summary>Method references</summary>

```{=html}
<p>Ruggles, C.L.N. (1999). <em>Astronomy in Prehistoric Britain and Ireland</em>.
Yale University Press.
</p>



```

</details>

**Interpretation and limits.** For a solar sight, the measured limb, civil time, timezone and instrument readings define a single observation. The useful independent check is recovery of a known terrestrial bearing from that observation.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Location, either a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> or a vector
containing the latitude, longitude and elevation of location, in this order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>az</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of azimuths. Use <code>ten</code> to convert to
decimal degrees if necessary.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>date</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Date of measurements as a string in the format: 'YYYY/MM/DD'</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>time</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Time of sun-sight measurement in the format: 'HH:MM:SS'</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>tz</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Timezone of input either as a known acronym (e.g. "GMT", "CET") or
a string with continent followed by country capital (e.g. "Europe/London").</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>az.sun</code></th><td><code>0</code></td><td><p>Measured azimuth of the sun. Defaults to zero.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>limb</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Measured limb of the sun. Options are <em>left</em>, <em>right</em>.
If missing the center of the sun will be used for calculations.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>alt</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Altitude, necessary for automatic declination calculation.
If missing and <em>loc</em> is a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> object then the altitude
will be automatically read from the horizon profile.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>name</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Names or labels to identify each measurement.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>ID</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>IDs or codes to identify each measurement.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>HWT.ID</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>HeyWhatsThat IDs relating to a previously generated
horizon profile for measurement.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A data frame with one row per observation. True.Azimuth is the corrected azimuth in degrees. The table also records the observed azimuth, solar azimuth, time and site coordinates. Where available it includes Altitude and Declination in degrees and the supplied identifiers.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/data-reduction.R`.
